subject: Proposed contract carveout: runtime telemetry forwarding & subprocessor whitelist
messages:
From: Alice Huang <alice.huang@medixhealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@medixhealth.com, legal@medixhealth.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA carveout: runtime telemetry forwarding + subprocessor whitelist

Hi David —

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal has reviewed the draft DPA and flagged two items that need explicit language before procurement can proceed: a) a carveout for forwarding runtime telemetry to our monitoring vendor for safety auditing; and b) an explicit whitelist of subprocessors used for telemetry processing (we need names + residency).

High level asks:
- Can Redwood agree to a narrow carveout that allows forwarding only metadata-level telemetry (no request/response payloads) to our monitoring partner?
- Provide the list of subprocessors that will see telemetry and their hosting regions.
- If possible, add an audit clause that gives us quarterly attestations of telemetry handling (summary form, not raw logs).

We attached a marked-up DPA (Medix-DPA-redline-v3.pdf) with proposed edits. Please confirm if Product & Security can sign off or if you need an exception path. Procurement would like to lock pricing this week.

Best,
Alice Huang
Sr. Counsel, Medix Health

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: alice.huang@medixhealth.com, procurement@medixhealth.com
Date: Thu, 24 Jun 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: DPA carveout: runtime telemetry forwarding + subprocessor whitelist

Olga / Karthik / Marissa —

Forwarding Medix's redline and asks. Key points we need to evaluate:
1) Medix requests a carveout permitting forwarding of runtime telemetry to their monitoring vendor, but explicitly restricts payloads ("metadata-only").
2) They require a named list of telemetry subprocessors and regions.
3) A quarterly attestation requirement (summary).

Product questions I want answered before we respond to Legal/Procurement:
- Marissa: what would be the product impact of conditioning telemetry forwarding to metadata-only? Any perf or SLO implications if we strip fields before forwarding? Is this a simple transformation or does it break existing observability pipelines?
- Karthik: can we produce a minimal subprocessor list limited to telemetry processors (exclude other infra)? Residency we can pull from inventory but confirm if any are EU-only.
- Olga: what's the security/legal tolerance for an attestation clause vs. a right-to-audit request? Would quarterly attestations be acceptable to Security, or do we need tighter wording?

They want to close the procurement window this week — I'm asking for a signoff path or an exception that the GRC team can approve. Please reply with concrete edits or a yes/no on acceptance.

Thanks,
David
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.ai>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: alice.huang@medixhealth.com, procurement@medixhealth.com
Date: Fri, 25 Jun 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA carveout: runtime telemetry forwarding + subprocessor whitelist

David —

Thanks for flagging. Quick take after an initial review and sync with Security: we can probably accept a limited carveout with these controls, but need the DPA language to be narrow and operationalized. Proposed guardrails: 

1) Definition: explicitly define "runtime telemetry" as non-PII metadata (latencies, error codes, anonymized model IDs, request size, geo-aggregates). No request/response content, no generated text.

2) Forwarding scope: allow forwarding to named monitoring vendors only; each vendor must be listed as a subprocessor in the DPA. If Medix asks to allow their vendor (Telemetry Integrations), we need its legal entity name and hosting regions.

3) Subprocessor list: we'll provide the telemetry-specific subprocessors (not full infra list). Format: vendor name + primary hosting region + purpose. This will be a short appendix. Karthik, please surface the current telemetry processors and residency.

4) Attestation vs. audit: Security prefers quarterly attestations (signed summary) for telemetry handling + one annual audit right (desk audit) triggered by a material incident. We should push back on open-ended audit access to raw logs. Olga thinks that meets compliance while limiting exposure.

5) Implementation: Marissa, product needs to confirm that we can implement metadata-only stripping as a routing transform before forwarding. If it's low effort, we can accept the clause with an operational note in the DPA requiring the transform. If it's moderate/high effort, we should propose an alternative: timeboxed pilot with Telemetry Integrations (30 days) before general availability.

Please see attached sketch: runtime-telemetry-diagram.png — shows where the strip/forward step would sit in our pipeline.

If we agree to the above, I'll prepare a narrow redline and return to Medix legal. If not, we should propose a compromise (pilot + attestation).

- Olga
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>

Cc: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 27 Jun 2027 16:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed contract carveout: runtime telemetry forwarding & subprocessor whitelist

Alice —

Thank you for the clear asks and the redline. We've scoped this internally and can offer the following path so procurement can proceed: 

1) Narrow carveout accepted: Redwood will allow forwarding of runtime telemetry strictly defined as metadata-only (see Olga's definition). We will not forward request/response payloads or generated outputs.

2) Subprocessor appendix: We will provide a telemetry subprocessor appendix listing the monitoring vendor(s) by legal entity and hosting region. For Telemetry Integrations, we request the vendor's legal name and endpoint residency confirmation — we have them on file as "Telemetry Integrations, Inc." (US primary region).

3) Attestation & audit: Redwood will provide quarterly attestations summarizing telemetry forwarding activity and controls. We will also accept one annual desk audit right limited to documentation and summary logs; raw logs will remain under Redwood custody and only shared under formal legal process.

4) Implementation / timeline: Product confirms the metadata-strip transform is a low-effort change (Marissa: 2 sprints to deliver a transform and config to route filtered telemetry). As a safety net, we'll run a 30-day pilot with the named vendor upon contract signature. Karthik will provide the telemetry subprocessor appendix by EOD 2027-06-28.

If Medix agrees to the above language, we'll send a narrow DPA redline for countersignature tomorrow and attach the subprocessor appendix. If you need any edits to the wording, Olga will lead the redline.

Next steps:
- Medix: confirm vendor legal name + acceptance of attestation/audit scope.
- David: circulate redline once Karthik provides appendix.
- Product/Security: prepare the pilot runbook.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — hoping this keeps procurement on schedule.

Best,
David Kim
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
